title: Trump’s Tariffs DON’T Cause Inflation — Jim Rickards Exposes Economic Truths & Musk Feud
summary: Blaze segment with Jim Rickards arguing tariffs are absorbed by importers and exporters rather than consumers, do not cause inflation or slow growth, and that debt only matters relative to GDP.

assertions.quote: So the point being tariffs don't cause inflation.
The one place it does not go is to the consumer

verdicts.note: Pass-through estimates for US tariffs run around 90% to importers and their customers; margins absorbed only a minority.

Border pass-through is about 90 percent, so exporters absorb little; domestic producers pass input tariffs into producer prices; and a 10 percent rise in tariff-induced pre-retail prices raises retail prices 5.6 percent, consistent with complete pass-through net of distribution margins rather than absorption in margins.

assertions.quote: if you could raise prices to consumers, you would just do it. You wouldn't need a tariff as an excuse.

verdicts.note: A tariff raises costs for every importer at once, shifting the whole market's price, unlike a single firm raising prices alone.

Regional business surveys found most tariff-paying firms had already passed at least some of the cost on through higher prices, and nearly half still planned further tariff-induced increases a year on.

assertions.quote: it doesn't slow the economy the way the mainstream economist said

verdicts.note: Most estimates put the 2025 tariffs at a drag of roughly half a point of GDP; no recession followed but growth was lower than otherwise.

assertions.quote: it has now been cut by more than half. And the big drop in imports seems to be where everyone's pointing.

verdicts.note: Imports fell in Q2 2025 after Q1 front-running, lifting measured GDP that quarter, but the 2025 goods deficit ended about equal to 2024.

assertions.quote: claiming that the Trump tariffs, they were going to tank the economy. So what's going on here? That's that's not the case right now

verdicts.note: No recession occurred in 2025, but prices rose and growth slowed; most mainstream forecasts predicted a drag, not a collapse.

assertions.quote: the debt is growing more slowly than the economy, which means the debt to GDP ratio is going down

verdicts.note: Debt dynamics depend on the gap between nominal growth and the deficit plus interest; this is standard public finance.
